item.title: New topological microscope tip reveals evidence of 2D altermagnetism
item.description: Researchers have fashioned a layered topological material into a scanning tunneling microscope (STM) tip that senses spin-related electronic states at atomic resolution.

item.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
item.description: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. item.title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
item.description: arXiv:2610.18953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge. item.title: Cryogenic Multiplexing Control Chip for Superconducting Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.19599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a scheme and design of cryogenic multiplexing control chip (MCC) which enables one microwave cable to control many superconducting qubits. Designed based on adjustable inductor, MCC is a non-reciprocal device which generates microwave signals between 4 and 8 GHz and constructs XY control circuit to operate qubits.
